name: Hilti Jaibot
summary: A battery-powered tracked robot that drills anchor holes in ceilings and walls from the digital drilling plan, located by a Hilti total station.

priceOther.market: Hong Kong CITF pre-approved list (subsidy price ceiling): Jaibot system with PLC 400 tablet, PLT 300 total station, TE 6-A22 rotary hammer, VC 5 vacuum, PM 30-MG laser, PS 50 detector, PD-E range meter, batteries, remote control, marker system and 2-year warranty

sellers.note: Contact form for Jaibot experts on the page. Trade press (2023) describes rental from Hilti with measurement concept, data preparation, training, support and an operator on request; an outright purchase is not described.
sellers.name: Hilti Deutschland AG

germany.statusNote: Offered in Germany by Hilti Deutschland AG on request; trade press describes rental from Hilti including measurement concept, data preparation, training, support and, if needed, the operator. No public price.

specs.label: Wall drilling height
specs.conditions: June 2022 Hilti release; the May 2023 release gives 1.2-4.8 m for both ceilings and walls

specs.label: Runtime
specs.conditions: up to, between charges, cordless (Hilti); trade press gives 8-10 h

specs.label: Output
specs.conditions: customer result (Geiger, obstacle-free new office building) quoted in the Hilti release

specs.label: Step it can cross
specs.conditions: single step, trade press report; it cannot climb stairs

specs.label: Positioning
specs.value: Hilti PLT 300 total station; PLC 400 tablet

specs.label: Base materials
specs.value: concrete ceilings and walls, metal composite (trapezoidal) ceilings

specs.label: Dust extraction
specs.conditions: integrated; optional upgrade for 30% more suction

notes: Semi-autonomous: an operator drives it between positions by remote control; drilling runs automatically.
Rubber-track drive; climbs a 15 cm step and tolerates 15° incline but cannot climb stairs (trade press). Delivered to site by crane in a special box.
Detects existing installations and adapts its arm movement; documents every hole in Hilti Cloud.

images.alt: Hilti Jaibot on tracks in a building under construction with an operator

evidence.task: Drilled 2,500 ceiling holes in eight days for acoustic baffles on a ceiling almost 5 m high (rented from Hilti)
evidence.where: Frietsch Gipser und Stukkateur, Wildpark-Stadion Karlsruhe, Germany

evidence.task: Drilled about 15,500 ceiling holes for anchors in an office building, over 1,000 per day
Drilling test against two crews on a live site: the laser-plus-hand team finished after 54 minutes, the conventional team after 63 and the robot team after 81
evidence.where: Burkhalter group (Alpha Plan AG, Marcel Hufschmid AG), Mobility Hub Zug Nord, Switzerland
evidence.note: A Hilti (Schweiz) sales engineer quoted in the post: the robot pays off from about four days of continuous use, about 2,000 holes.
